papers.title_en: A Physics-Flavored Transformer Network for Parametrizing Contraction Dynamics of Engineered Skeletal Muscle Tissues
papers.evidence: 面向药物筛选的深度学习物理风味代理，用于组织收缩动力学
papers.tldr: 工程化骨骼肌组织（ESM）的表征常依赖峰值力等简单指标，忽视收缩动力学信息，而机理模型因数学复杂难以推广。为此提出物理风味神经网络（PFNN），将拉伸指数物理模型嵌入CNN-Transformer，直接从力-时间曲线提取物理参数。采用混合训练范式：先在合成数据上建立物理直觉，再通过无监督自对齐适配未标注的真实数据。在多种收缩表型及Duchenne肌营养不良症模型上实现高保真参数化，弥合理想生物物理与噪声体外数据的鸿沟，为高通量生物物理研究提供可扩展工具。
papers.abstract_en: Engineered Skeletal Muscle Tissues (ESMs) have become a key structure for biomedical disease modeling and pharmacological screening, yet their functional characterization often relies on simplistic metrics like peak force, discarding critical kinetic information. This is partially due to the high level of mathematical complexity which mechanistic models introduce to capture these dynamics. Hence, exactly the complexity prevents scalable application and widespread adaptation in the field. Here we present a Physics-Flavored Neural Network (PFNN) that automates the kinetic phenotyping of ESMs. Our architecture integrates a stretched-exponential physical model into a CNN-Transformer, enabling the extraction of physically meaningful parameters directly from force-time profiles. To address the scarcity of labeled biological data, we employ a hybrid training paradigm: the model develops a "physical intuition" on synthetic data before undergoing unsupervised self-alignment on unlabeled real-world measurements. Our results demonstrate that this physics-flavored approach achieves high-fidelity parameterization across diverse contractile phenotypes and cell lines, including Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy models. Our scalable, self-improving pipeline bridges the gap between idealized biophysics and noisy \emph{in vitro} data, providing a robust tool for high-throughput biophysical research.
